ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: Muscle will contract when stimulated, and the changes in electric potential inside and outside the muscle cell membrane before and after the muscle is stimulated are the same as the potential changes in nerve fibers. Now take two fresh nerve-muscle specimens, and place the nerve of the left specimen on the muscle of the right specimen; at this time the nerve fiber is connected with the muscle cell (during the experiment the specimens are moistened with physiological saline), as shown in the figure. In the figure, ② and ④ refer to the junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells; these junctions are similar to synaptic structures. Stimulating ① can cause the right muscle to contract, and the left muscle also contracts along with it. Among ①, ②, ③, and ④, which ones can conduct excitation (write the labels)?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, there are left and right nerve-muscle specimens. In the right specimen, there is a nerve fiber above the right muscle; ① is labeled near the position on the right nerve fiber receiving “S stimulation,” and ② is labeled at the junction where the right nerve contacts the right muscle. In the left specimen, there is also a nerve fiber above the left muscle; ③ is labeled near the nerve fiber segment placed on the right muscle, and ④ is labeled at the junction between the left nerve and the left muscle. Then reason: The question stem states that ② and ④ are junctions between nerve fibers and muscle cells, and their structures are similar to synapses. The propagation of excitation on the same nerve fiber or the same excitable cell membrane is called “excitation conduction”; whereas excitation passing from a nerve cell to a muscle cell through a nerve-muscle junction belongs to “excitation transmission,” and is not called excitation conduction. Therefore, ① and ③ are located on nerve fibers and can conduct excitation; ② and ④ are junctions, where excitation transmission occurs.
